React Native and Expo

Components for React Native.

The Colibri catalog, rebuilt for phones: every components and ready-made screens, themed from one hue. No build step, no configuration, and two ways to use it.

Light no dependencies

Everything that needs only React Native itself: most of the catalog. Works in any project and in Expo Go with nothing else to install.

npm install @colibri-kit/native
import { Button, BottomSheet } from "@colibri-kit/native";

Full 4 libraries

Light, plus the components that need a library: finger-driven sheets, rows and lists (Reanimated and Gesture Handler), line and pie charts and an icon set (SVG), and bars that fit the notch (Safe Area Context).

npm install @colibri-kit/native
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler react-native-svg react-native-safe-area-context
import { Button, BottomSheet, LineChart } from "@colibri-kit/native/full";

The two share names and props. A component that exists in both, such as BottomSheet, is the finger-driven version in Full, so moving from Light to Full is a change of import path. You can also take one piece at a time: @colibri-kit/native/gestures, /svg or /safe-area, each needing only its own library. In the list below, a card marked Full names the libraries it needs; unmarked cards are Light.

Pick a component below to try it on the phone, then switch to Code for a sample you can paste. The phone runs the real component code in your browser through react-native-web. Documentation on GitHub.
